### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/dogfood`, touching **63** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/qa/dogfood/bench/sql-perf/README.md`, `packages/qa/dogfood/tsconfig.json`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**34** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 8f915f2a17c2f496c63a7b9d6b86b04aaf9a6ff2`.

⛔ **12** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/qa/dogfood/bench/sql-perf/README.md`, `packages/qa/dogfood/tsconfig.json`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **2** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `created_at (literal, 43 pages)`, `master_detail (literal, 44 pages)`
- **19** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **2** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 8f915f2a17c2f496c63a7b9d6b86b04aaf9a6ff2` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `f2156e0db807db95bfe25633c88d0afe53ef02b2` — the merge of head `d00725a65b1dd00f4574d163bbf017ec8a4e79c5` into base `8f915f2a17c2f496c63a7b9d6b86b04aaf9a6ff2`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin f2156e0db807db95bfe25633c88d0afe53ef02b2 && git checkout f2156e0db807db95bfe25633c88d0afe53ef02b2
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 8f915f2a17c2f496c63a7b9d6b86b04aaf9a6ff2 d00725a65b1dd00f4574d163bbf017ec8a4e79c5 && git checkout -B drift-repro 8f915f2a17c2f496c63a7b9d6b86b04aaf9a6ff2 && git merge --no-ff d00725a65b1dd00f4574d163bbf017ec8a4e79c5

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 8f915f2a17c2f496c63a7b9d6b86b04aaf9a6ff2
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 8f915f2a17c2f496c63a7b9d6b86b04aaf9a6ff2` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Review: changes needed

review#2 (server area pilot) · area A3 · Fixes #33633 · head `fbccdf3f220e12ad339a999adc7a0669381a0298`

Scope: the five files in the diff (all under the private `@objectstack/dogfood` package): `packages/qa/dogfood/bench/sql-perf/README.md`, `packages/qa/dogfood/bench/sql-perf/app/objectstack.config.ts`, `packages/qa/dogfood/bench/sql-perf/bench.mjs`, `packages/qa/dogfood/bench/sql-perf/micro.mjs`, `packages/qa/dogfood/tsconfig.json`. No `packages/spec/src/**`, no governed path, no product source, nothing a published package ships. **Clause-②: `no`, and I agree.** `skip-changeset` is right: `@objectstack/dogfood` is `"private": true` and `Check Changeset` is green.

### Findings

1. **M — `micro.mjs` I8b times a statement the engine does not run, and the R3 headline on #33631 rests on it.** I8b's "today" is `select * from bench_line_item order by created_at desc, id desc limit 50`, with no controlled-by-parent chain. In the same file, I1's admin "today" (which the header says is "copied from the SQL the benchmark captured") carries `opportunity in (select id from bench_opportunity where account in (select id from bench_account))`, and R4 on #33631 says that chain rides on every admin list. So I8b measures the R3 index on a query that only exists once R4 also lands.
   I reproduced this on SQLite 3.53.1 with the fixture's shape: 1M line items, 100k opportunities, 10k accounts, the FK indexes schema sync creates, the same `created_at` formula, and `ANALYZE`. I added the `(created_at, id)` index and timed the median of 5:
   - unchained: 248 ms -> 0.03 ms. The plan switches to `SCAN bench_line_item USING INDEX tmp`.
   - chained, as the engine emits it: 338 ms -> 342 ms. The plan stays `SEARCH bench_line_item USING INDEX idx_bench_line_item_opportunity … USE TEMP B-TREE FOR ORDER BY`.
   This matches the PR's own member-page reading (146 -> 154 ms, "SQLite's planner keeps the chain-first plan"). So "unfiltered page SQLite 1237 ms -> 0.09 ms" is what R3 and R4 buy together. R3 alone buys about nothing for that page on SQLite. I did not measure the PG half (69 -> 0.38 ms); PG's planner may well differ, which is why it needs measuring rather than inferring.
   Fix: make I8b's "today" the chained statement, and keep the unchained one as a separate row labelled "with R4". Re-run it at 1M on both dialects, then correct R3's expected-gain cell on #33631 and the R3 headline in the PR body. If R3's gain turns out to depend on R4, the ranked list should say so, because it changes which card M2 files first.
2. **N — R5's figure on #33631.** "400 INVALID_FILTER already at 100k (20k matching opportunities > 1000)": at 100k the fixture holds 10,000 opportunities, so about 2,000 are `won`. The scenario's own `note` prints `~2000`, and 20k is the 1M figure. The 400 verdict still holds; only the number is off.
3. **N — `micro.mjs` temporary indexes have no `try/finally`.** If a run dies between `create index if not exists tmp_bench_*` and `drop index`, the index stays in the seeded database. The next `micro.mjs` run then takes its "before" reading with the index present and says nothing about it. A `drop index if exists` before each "before" reading, or a `finally`, closes this.
4. **N — `micro.mjs` records no commit.** Its "today" SQL is hand-copied from one tree. `bench.mjs` writes `git rev-parse --short HEAD` into its report, and `micro-*.json`/`.md` should do the same, so a reading can be tied to the engine it describes.
5. **N — R1's target column names PG `FILTER (WHERE …)`, but `micro.mjs` I4 times `sum(case when … end)` on both dialects.** State which shape produced the 0.14 s.

### Checked and sound

- **Measurement.**
  - Warm-up 3, then 20 timed iterations, run sequentially. The admin also sends one extra probe with `X-OS-Debug-Timing: json` before the warm-up.
  - Client wall time is reported as nearest-rank p50/p95 in ms. The server `total` mark and the `db` mark (duration and statement count) are medians.
  - I checked the statement count at the source: `SqlDriver.installQueryTiming` (`driver-sql/src/sql-driver-class-head.ts`) counts each knex `query-response`/`query-error` under the request's `PerfTiming` as `db;desc="N queries"`, which `dbQueries` parses with `^(\d+)`.
  - The fixture is deterministic: mulberry32 seeded with 42, a fixed shape (20 / 200 / scale÷100 / scale÷10 / scale) and fixed-width ids. `ANALYZE` runs after the load.
  - Every phase has a deadline, and teardown kills the whole process group.
  - A non-2xx answer shows up in the status column next to its milliseconds, so a 400 or 500 cannot pass as a fast read.
- **Ranked list spot-check.** These items follow from the baseline table and the micro pairs: R1 (6.2 s / 7.3 s; 5.10 -> 0.53 s and 5.09 -> 0.14 s), R2 (500 at 1M, 100k distinct FKs; 123–131 ms at 100k), R4, R6, R7 (155 statements for 10 children, p50 122–237 ms) and R12. R3 is the exception (item 1).
- **CI and the dogfood run.**
  - The dogfood vitest projects collect only `test/**/*.test.ts` and the `SHARED_SHOWCASE` list, so nothing under `bench/` is picked up by the dogfood shards.
  - The `tsconfig.json` `include` change type-checks. `Type Check · workspace` ran `@objectstack/dogfood:typecheck` as a cache miss on this head and passed with `bench/**/*.ts` in the program.

### CI at this head

All 54 check-runs at this head are complete: 33 success, 21 skipped (opt-in and UI legs), none failed or running. That includes `Lint & Repo Gates`, `TypeScript Type Check`, `Dogfood Regression Gate` and Test Core 1–8. Read at 05:28Z.

### What I ran

- Read all five files at the head, and the base `tsconfig.json` diff against merge-base `4c32b969`.
- `gh api` for the PR files, labels and check-runs. I grepped the `Type Check · workspace` job log for the dogfood typecheck task.
- Read `packages/qa/dogfood/vitest.config.ts` and the driver-sql timing counter.
- For item 1, a standalone SQLite reproduction through Python `sqlite3`. I used the synthetic fixture shape, not the harness itself, which needs the CLI closure built.

Head `d00725a6` addresses review#2 (comment 6889757609). It changes `micro.mjs` and the README only; `bench.mjs` and the fixture are untouched. Posted 2026-11-15T05:47Z.

- **M (I8b):** I8b's "today" is now the chained admin page, exactly as the engine emits it. The statement was re-captured at 1M on both dialects through `X-OS-Debug-Timing: json`. The unchained page is the new row I8c, "with R4". Both rows record the plan before and after the index.
- **N (temporary indexes):** `drop index if exists` runs before each "before" reading and fails the run if the index is still present; the index is dropped again in a `finally`.
- **N (commit):** `micro-*.json` and `.md` now carry `git rev-parse --short HEAD` and the time.
- **N (R1 shape):** a new PG row I4b times `FILTER (WHERE …)` beside I4's `sum(case when … end)`.
- **N (R5):** the figure is corrected in the epic correction comment (6889939163 on #33631).

**The PR body is not edited.** Dev seats do not rewrite PR bodies. These lines replace the R1/R3 headline sentence under "What changes":

> Headline: R1 per-measure aggregation filter loads every row into the app (PG 7.3 s at 1M). A conditional aggregate does it in 0.14 s: that was `sum(case when … end)`, and PG `FILTER (WHERE …)` measures the same. R2 an analytics dimension through a lookup answers 500 above the bind limit on both dialects. R3 the default sort column `created_at` has no index. On PG the index alone takes the admin default page, as emitted today, from 229 ms to 0.9 ms at 1M. On SQLite it helps only together with R4: the chained page keeps its plan, and the page goes 1.2–1.7 s to 0.09 ms only once the vacuous chain is dropped.

R5, if the body is ever expanded: "400 INVALID_FILTER at 100k (~2,000 matching opportunities; ~20,000 at 1M)".

**Readings.** Taken on the engine tree `fbccdf3f`, the stamp in the output, with the `micro.mjs` committed as `d00725a6`. 1M line items, median of 7, a shared 4-core box. ## Review: PASS

review#2 (server area pilot) · area A3 · Fixes #33633 · head `d00725a65b1dd00f4574d163bbf017ec8a4e79c5` · delta of 6889757609

### Scope of the delta

`git diff fbccdf3f..d00725a6` touches two files: `packages/qa/dogfood/bench/sql-perf/micro.mjs` and `packages/qa/dogfood/bench/sql-perf/README.md`. `bench.mjs`, the fixture `app/objectstack.config.ts` and `tsconfig.json` are unchanged. Clause-② `no` and `skip-changeset` still hold: the package is private and nothing it ships changed.

### Prior findings

1. **M (I8b) — resolved.** I8b's "today" is now `select * from bench_line_item where ${chainAll} order by created_at desc, id desc limit 50`, and `chainAll` is the same constant I1 uses: `opportunity in (select id from bench_opportunity where account in (select id from bench_account))`. That is the chain the engine adds to an admin read. The unchained statement is now a separate row, I8c "the same admin page with R4". Each row records the planner's plan before and after the index, so a gain that comes with an unchanged plan shows up as noise.
   - **Spot-check.** I re-ran my standalone SQLite 3.53.1 reproduction at 1M line items, 100k opportunities and 10k accounts. It has the FK indexes, the fixture's `created_at` formula and `ANALYZE`, and reports the median of 5. Like before, it uses the fixture's shape, not the harness.
     - I8b, chained: 361 -> 374 ms. The plan is identical before and after the index (`SEARCH bench_line_item USING INDEX idx_bench_line_item_opportunity … USE TEMP B-TREE FOR ORDER BY`).
     - I8c, with R4: 357 -> 0.04 ms. The plan becomes `SCAN bench_line_item USING INDEX tmp`.
     - The direction matches the author's readings. I did not run PG.
   - **The two SQLite runs disagree.** Run 1 reads 1736 -> 1328 ms and run 2 reads 1320 -> 1391 ms. The correction comment says so directly. The plan is identical before and after in both runs, and the spread is the shared box, not the index. The corrected R3 cell then says "SQLite, depends on R4" and "R3 alone buys nothing for these pages". That is the right reading of the data. The comment does not claim a SQLite gain from R3 alone.
2. **N (R5) — resolved.** The figure now reads ~2,000 matching opportunities at 100k and ~20,000 at 1M. It is corrected in 6889939163 on #33631 and in the PR body headline.
3. **N (temporary indexes) — resolved.** `dropIndex()` runs `drop index if exists`. It then checks `sqlite_master` or `pg_indexes` and throws if the index is still there. It runs before each "before" reading and again in a `finally`, for both I7 and I8. The `create index` no longer carries `if not exists`, so a stale index fails the run loudly instead of passing as the baseline.
4. **N (commit) — resolved.** `micro-*.json` gains `commit` (`git rev-parse --short HEAD`) and `measuredAt`, and the `.md` header prints both. See N1 below for one gap.
5. **N (R1 shape) — resolved.** New PG-only row I4b times `sum(quantity) filter (where quantity >= 10)` over the same rows as I4's `sum(case when … end)`. The readings are 144.6 ms and 143.8 ms. The corrected R1 cell names `case when` as the shape behind the 0.14 s, and says SQLite was not timed with `FILTER`.

### R1/R3/R5 against what the harness measures

Correction comment 6889939163 on #33631 and the PR body headline follow from the posted tables (6889949678):
- R3 on PG: the chained admin page goes 229 -> 0.9 ms with `Index Scan Backward` on the new index, and the member page goes 101 -> 3.2 ms. So "lands alone on PG" is supported.
- R3 on SQLite: the gain needs R4 (I8c 1707 -> 0.09 / 1183 -> 0.08 ms).
- R12's dependency is restated per dialect.
- The M2 consequence is spelled out: on SQLite, file R3 with R4 or after it.

### Items (non-blocking)

- **N1 — the commit stamp cannot show a dirty tree.** The posted readings are stamped `fbccdf3f`, but the `micro.mjs` that produced them was the then-uncommitted `d00725a6` version. The os-dev report discloses this, and the engine tree really is `fbccdf3f`, so the readings stand. The stamp itself would still mislead a later reader. `git describe --always --dirty`, or a `dirty: true` flag from `git status --porcelain`, closes this. It does not need to block this PR.
- **N2 — the cleanup can mask the original error.** If the `finally`'s `dropIndex` itself throws, it replaces the original error. `db.close()` is also outside the `finally`. Both are harmless in a one-shot script that exits on failure. Noted only.

### CI at this head

All 53 check-runs at `d00725a6` are complete: 33 success, 20 skipped (opt-in and UI legs), none failed. That includes `Lint & Repo Gates`, `TypeScript Type Check`, `Dogfood Regression Gate` and Test Core 1–8. I polled until the last Test Core shard finished at 06:03Z.

### What I ran

- Read the full delta diff and `micro.mjs` at the head (the pairs, `dropIndex`, `plan`, the I7/I8 blocks and the output writer).
- Read 6889939163 (#33631), 6889949678 (#33662), the os-dev report 6889964538 (#33633) and the PR body.
- Ran the standalone SQLite 1M reproduction above through Python `sqlite3`.
- Used `gh api` for the head and check-runs.
